LEONC'O, u.O., fcps, EPSGS Municipal Mayor Municipality of Brooke's Point Province of Palawan Dear Mayor Leoncio: This concerns your' letter requesting our approval for you to practice your profession as a surgeon after office hours and during emergency cåses given the fåct, as you represented, that your municipality has only two (2) practicing surgeons including yourself and that your municipality's two hospitals provide medical services also to patients coming from nearby municipalities. While we commend your noble intention to be of service to your people not only as a municipal mayor but also as doctor, however please be inlörmed that we have already addressed a similar issue on DILG Opinion NO. 99, series of 2010, where we opined that mayors and governors are prohibited from practicing lheir profession, other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives, in accordance with Section 90 of the Local Government Code Q/' 1991 (RA 7160). Accordingly, in Chua vs. Atty No. 5738, February 12, 2008, the Supreme COLIrt held that the prohibition emphasizes the need for local chief executives to render filll time service as such, so that they should devote all their time and attention to the performance of their official duties. However, please note that we also pointed out in the aforesaid opinion that, if one's being a doctor would only be necessarily incidental to his being a local chief executive, no exemption is needed for him to act as a doctor. His duties as a local chief executive should be the primordial consideration While hi9 action as a doctor a direct consequence thereof. Given this underlying principle, we reiterate our view herein, that you may exercise your profession as a surgeon but only within your municipality and during emergency cases. We hope that we have enlightened you on lhe matter. Very truly yours, JESUS B. DOQUE •V Director Ill IS: 2 /rb-l.qbfol.der
